Message from the 
Chairman 
In 2020, MB continued to be recognized as one of the 
groups of enterprises with over VND 10 trillion profit 
and listed as one of Top 30 of largest enterprises in 
Vietnam (according to VNR500 rating)
Colonel General Le Huu Duc
Chairman of The Board of Directors
All areas of world economics in 2020 
were heavily affected by Covid-19 
pandemic. Despite the high pandemic 
impact, under flexible and strong 
leadership of the Party and the 
Government of Vietnam, the economy 
has recovered to normal conditions 
and has become a highlight when GDP 
growth rate was among the highest 
group in the world, accomplishing 
both economic growth and disease 
control goals. Specifically, GDP in 
2020 grew by 2.91%, while global GDP 
growth 2020 according to World Bank 
forecast was at 2.5%; Vietnam CPI was 
stable at around 3.23%; total social 
investment was at VND 2,164.5 trillion, 
increased by 5.7% compared to that of 
2019 and equivalent to 34.4% of GDP.
The State Bank of Vietnam continued 
operating 
a 
strong 
and 
flexible 
monetary policy in 2020: Total liquidity 
grew by 12.56%; capital mobilization 
increased by 12.87%; Credit balance 
growth was at 10.14%; the State 
Bank lowered the interest rates three 
times; exchange rates were sustained; 
non-performing loans were strictly 
controlled.
Although 
the 
Covid-19 
pandemic 
has broke out and affected Vietnam 
since the beginning of the year, 
MB Board of Directors has applied 
technology to implement a variety 
of flexible meetings to ensure that 
executive and administrative activities 
are kept as usual operation and MB 
business practices continue to occur 
continuously and seamlessly. 
The period of social distancing was 
also an opportunity for MB to review 
the entire system, fine-tune the process 
and strengthen HR and operational 
quality. 
Running 
by 
the 
motto 
“Foundation Strengthening, Digital 
Transformation, 
Comprehensive, 
Efficient and Sustainable Growth” 
and the principle “Rule of Law”, 
pursuing the strategic vision “To be 
the most convenient Bank”, targeting 
the goals of “TOP 5 in operational 
quality 
and 
efficiency, 
leading 
digital applications”; the entire MB 
system was strongly determined 
to 
successfully 
accomplish 
the 
targets entrusted by the General 
Shareholder’s Meeting, specifically:
•	 By the end of 2020, total MB 
consolidated assets reached VND 
494,982 billion; charter capital 
reached VND 27,988 billion; The 
Group’s before tax profit reached 
VND 10,688 billion, resulting in 
MB to be in the list of Vietnamese 
enterprises with the profit of over 
VND 10 trillion for the second 
consecutive year. Risks were 
strictly controlled; the Group’s 
non-performing loan (NPL) ratio 
was approximately 1.09% (the 
Bank only was just 0.92%); non-
performing loan coverage ratio of 
the credit loss provision reached 
158.9%; 
safeguard 
requirements 
established by the State Bank were 
complied.
•	 In 2020, MB completed charter capital raising program 
and treasury stocks distribution which were approved by 
the Annual General Meeting of Shareholders.
•	 Notably, despite common difficulties caused by Covid-19 
pandemic, subsidaries  actively implemented business 
solutions to maintain their market positions (MBS was 
in TOP 3 IB consulting companies, MIC was in TOP 6 
companies with the biggest non-life insurance market 
share). Total profit before taxes in 2020 of subsidiaries 
was VND1,418.8 billion, increased by 19% compared to 
2019 and achieved 124% of the planned target. The good 
performance of subsidiaries   significantly contributed to 
the Group’s results: specifically, their profit contributed 
to the overall achievement of the Group’s planned target 
considering a smaller profit from parent Bank due to 
activities supporting the customers affected by Covid-19 
pandemic under the general policies of the Government 
of Vietnam and the State Bank; the subsidiaries  also 
helped the Group be recognized as TOP 1 company with 
the highest sales of insurance through bank (Bancas). 
MB has invested substantially and systematically in 
information technology; this has been the foundation for 
MB to lead in digital transformation, achieve breakthrough 
growth in the number of customers conducting transactions 
via digital channels since 2017. Specifically, MB provides 2 
products: (1) MBBank APP for individual customers (received 
Sao Khue Award in 2019) - which overpassed many other 
international famous apps  in terms of downloads from 
App store in Vietnam at times and (2) BIZ MBBank for 
enterprise customers (received Sao Khue Award in 2020). 
In 2020, MB had 1.9 million new MBBank APP customers 
and 40 thousand new MBBank BIZ customers; the ratio of 
digital transactions was at 85%. Based on this outstanding 
historical data, the number and ratio of digital customers 
will surely grow even stronger in the upcoming years. In 
2020, along with consistent brand identity changes across 
the parent bank and subsidiaries, the opening of MB’s new 
splendid headquarters with various smart utilities at 18 Le 
Van Luong Street has taken MB brand to a new heights. Also 
during the year, MB expanded and deepened partnerships 
with many prestigious domestic and foreign corporates 
and Groups. These partnerships promise more business 
development, expanding customer portfolios and value 
chains, bringing about higher value to MB ‘s shareholders 
and customers.
In 2020, MB was honored to receive a number of major 
awards such as: Emulation flags from the Prime Minister, 
the Minister of Defense, the Governor of State Bank, etc. At 
the same time, MB also actively participated in programs 
supporting businesses affected by Covid-19 pandemic, 
other nation-wide charity and social security programs, and 
the Bank has been recognized as a community responsible 
bank.
In 2021, the world economy is forecast to grow at 
approximately 4% while Vietnam’s GDP and CPI at  6.5% and 
4%, respectively, experiencing a strong recovery. Numerous 
sectors are expected to achieve better growth rate in 2021 
including private property/FDI/personal consumption/
retail/import - export/logistic. The State Bank continues to 
operate a flexible monetary policy; credit is forecast to grow 
by 12%; exchange rate is maintained in stable manner and 
NPLs are strictly controlled. In 2021, the State Bank’s capital 
adequacy ratio regulations are in effect, gearing towards 
Basel 2 standards.
The year 2021 is the final year for MB to complete its  2017-
2021 phase strategic goals and establish new strategies for 
2022-2026 phase. The MB Board has set the motto for 2021 
as “Digital Boost; Retail Breakthrough; Safety - Efficiency”, 
pursuing the vision “to be the most convenient Bank”, 
ranking “No.1 in Digital Banking”; listing “Top 3 in Retail 
Banking Vietnam”, maintaining “Rule of Law”. Accordingly, 
Digital Banking continues to be a key and prerequisite 
condition for completing current phase strategic goals, and 
the premise and foundation for MB’s next phase strategies. 
In the context of Covid-19 pandemic with hidden and 
complex risks and growing tough competition between 
banks, MB Board of Directors, Supervisory Board and 
Board of Management are determined to make best efforts 
to implement flexible and innovative solutions to further 
enhance MB service quality, complete 2017 - 2021 strategic 
goals, bringing higher value to customers and shareholders.
MB would like to thank and look forward to receiving 
direction, support from Central Military Commission, 
Ministry of Defense and other ministries and departments 
as well as support and cooperation from strategic partners 
who are the world’s leading companies in financial 
sectors such as Shinsei Bank (Japan), Ageas Insurance 
Group (Belgium) ... the support, love and trust of millions 
of customers, shareholders, and the dedication of tens of 
thousands of MB staff members across the system. MB is 
committed to ongoing efforts and believes that aspirations 
to become “a strong financial group of regional and global 
class” will soon be realized.
Colonel General Le Huu Duc
Chairman of The Board of Directors

From an initial idea to formulate a credit institution 
to serve military enterprises with the task of 
commercial production during the preintegration 
period, on 4 November 1994, Military Commercial 
Joint Stock Bank was established with a capital 
of nearly VND20 billion, 25 employees and a 
single point of transaction at 28A Dien Bien Phu 
Street, Hanoi.
The first ten years (1994-2004) was a period of 
“exploration” to shape the operation’s motto, set 
the business strategy and define the brand. Being 
determined with its long-term objectives and vision, 
MB flexibly adopted robust solutions to learn from 
experience and formulate its financial capacity, 
affirmed its role and made significant contribution 
to development of the economy, contributing 
to fulfilment of the economic – defence duties 
of the Army. MB confidently overcame the Asian 
financial crisis in 1997 and was the only profitable 
bank; in 2004, the year of its tenth anniversary of 
foundation, MB’s total mobilised capital increased 
to more than 500 times the initial amount, its total 
assets reached more than VND7,000 billion and its 
profits exceeded VND500 billion; and MB opened 
its state-of-the-art head office at 3 Lieu Giai Street, 
Ba Dinh District, Hanoi.
Process of formation 
and development
2010, MB started to develop the strategy for the 
new period 2011 – 2015, with an expectation to 
win the position in the top 3 list of joint stock 
commercial banks that are not predominantly 
owned by the State. This was also a very difficult 
period of the economy. Due to impact of the world 
economic crisis, the banking sector implemented 
a drastic restructuring process; several banks saw 
decreases in profits and were even mergered or 
disappeared from the market. In this context, MB 
remained steadfast in its sustainable and safe 
development strategy to win the leading position 
with respect to multiple financial indicators, and 
met its target of winning the position in the top 
3 list two years ahead of schedule – in 2013. Due 
to its achievements, in 2014, MB was honoured to 
receive the First-Class Labour Medal. Subsequently 
in 2015, MB was honoured to be conferred the title 
“Hero of Labour”.
This period marked an important turning point, 
creating the foundation for vigorous development 
in subsequent years. During this period, MB adopted 
an array of comprehensive reform solutions from 
expansion of its operation scale, development of its 
network, investment in technology, strengthening 
of personnel, orientation to customers with the 
segregation between the management function 
of the Head Office and the business function of 
branches, and re-organisation of business units by
individual client, SME client, treasury, etc. It could 
be said that the period 2005 – 2009 laid a solid 
foundation for MB to accelerate implementation 
of its strategic initiatives, enabling itself to become 
one of the current Vietnamese leading financial 
institutions. 2009 marked MB’s fifteen years of 
development when it was granted the Third-Class 
Labour Medal by the President of Vietnam.
These are four important years of the new strategic 
phase of 2017-2021. During this time, MB has 
embraced the vision “To be the most convenient 
bank”. In particular, the goal of 2021 is to be listed 
as Top 5 Vietnamese banking systems in business 
efficiency, reliability and digitalization.
Recently, MB has grown strongly and made 
enormous progress in business, accomplished 
successfully 
tasks 
and 
targets. 
Especially, 
considerable attentions have been paid to 
synchronously and drastically implement strategic 
projects on digital transformation. In 2020, MB 
launched its new and modern headquarters at 18 
Le Van Luong, Trung Hoa Ward, Cau Giay District, 
Hanoi City. At the same time, it was presented by 
the Government Prime Minister with emulation flag 
for leading the banking competition in Viêtnam. 
MB is currently one of top 13 income tax payers 
among Vietnamese corporates and one of top 5 
among Vietnamese banks.

bank governance in line with international standards, compliance with Circular

to cover all critical risks including the risks assessed at pillar 1 - Credit Risk,

on the bank register under normal business scenarios and stress test scenarios. 
The capital shall provide sufficient provisions to the business plan in the coming 
3-year phase. Furthermore, the Bank successfully identified the capital buffering 
level and specific solutions to operate safely and efficiently in the unfavorable 
market developments.
By setting up a solid risk management platform along with business operation 
goals, risk management at MB has been promoted by investing in systems, 
human resources, implementing tool risk measurement model and tools, 
improving data quality, process optimization, especially applying the results 
of credit rating model (A Score/B Score); Analyzing customer’s behavior during 
appraisal, approval, cross-selling, up-selling, providing credit for personal, micro 
SME customers (Retail) to speed up service delivery; simplifying the process and 
procedure to increase customer experience, understanding profoundly customer 
needs; improving credit quality to contribute to transforming retail structure for 
MB (In 2020 the retail credit growth accounted for more than 50% of the total 
outstanding loans and was the main drivers for MB growth).
In 2021, in addition to the goal of enhancing the bank’s profitability; ensuring the 
bank safe and efficient operation, MB continues to pioneer applying advanced 
standards, practice, and models in risk management to ensure optimization of 
MB assets, promoting and protecting the business value and outcomes to make 
differences in the market.

The senior supervisory role and three-layer protection model under regulations 
of Circular 13 by SBV and the Basel Committee practices are applied 
comprehensively and effectively in MB administrative operations and internal 
control. Responsibilities of Board of Directors and CEO for internal control, risk 
management, adequacy assessment, and internal audit are standardized to 
ensure independent roles; an individual/entity shall not involve in “executive” and 
“administration” at the same time;
MB organizes its entire management system with 3 layers of protection to ensure 
clear functionalities and duties of the units, improve the sense of responsibility 
of the whole Bank in identifying, evaluating, monitoring, and controlling risks. In 
particular, activities with potential risks of conflicts of interest in sales, appraisal, 
approval, and credit support are performed by independent units to ensure 
objectivity and transparency. At the same time, to achieve good control of risk, 
restriction of errors and mistakes, MB implements modern technology systems 
locating at the Headquarters with functions of credit appraisal, approval, 
support; accounting - financing, human resources, and information technology. 
Accordingly, MB branches and businesses can maximize resource utilization for 
business development, while ensuring that risks are controlled as business scales 
up and customer volume grows.
Consolidated risk management framework ensures comprehensive management 
of key risk types in the Bank’s operations (credit risks, operational risks, market 
risks, liquidity risks, interest rate risks on bank books, technology risks, centralized 
risks, risk of default, etc.) according to good international practices of Basel 
Committee, COSO, and ISO. Risk management policies and taste are documented, 
specifically stated, and fully identified in MB’s business operations. Critical risk 
management principles, framework, thresholds, and limits are established and 
periodically monitored to ensure alignment with business status and taste.
In addition to the traditional risk management, MB quickly integrated IT and 
digital banking risk management in the context of the technology era, to ensure 
risk management going in line with tight management of the Bank’s new moves. 
MB is one of the first banks applying new technologies for business and risk 
management such as EKYC, RPA, API, and Micro-services, OCR, Autotest… At 
the same time, MB has adopted comprehensive information security measures, 
information technology risk management from people, regulatory policies, 
standards, processes, and information security solutions. MB has been applying 
the best international standards for managing this type of risk: Standards of 
COBIT, ITIL, ISO 27001, etc. MB also cooperated with IBM’s strategic partner to 
implement a comprehensive information technology transformation project to 
enhance service capabilities, ensure stable, accurate operation, system safety, 
and investment resource efficiency.
In addition, MB has gradually established a framework of fraud risk management, 
analyzing data to detect fraud, to pro-actively prevent, early detect fraud (if any), 
minimize financial loss as well as negative impact on the reputation and image 
of the bank and protect the rights of customers.
In parallel with strengthening the risk management framework at the Bank, MB 
has basically established a risk management framework for its subsidiaries. The 
close connection between risk management of the bank and that of subsidiaries 
ensures that strategies and policies on risks are implemented holistically, 
appropriately and consistently throughout the Group.

Activities of the 
Supervisory Board 
in 2020
Supervisory Board coordinated well with the 
Board of Directors in the consolidation of 
Supervisory Board activities in accordance 
with laws, internal regulations, and advanced 
practices. Successfully completed Supervisory 
Board’s plan of 2020 which was approved by 
General Meeting of Shareholders with following 
contents:
In 2020, it was difficult and challenging for the economy in general and 
the banking sector in particular. It is also a year that marks strong moves 
of banking systems in administration and operations. In 2020, MB strongly 
invested in and implemented digital transformation solutions to be in 
line with the 2019–2021 phase strategy, contributing to the successful 
completion of the business plan approved by the General Meeting of 
Shareholders.
Supervisory Board coordinated with Board of Directors to prepare and submit 
to General Meeting of Shareholders to approve one member to MB Supervisory 
Board. Shortly after the General Meeting, Supervisory Board met and voted one 
Supervisory Board Vice Chairwoman, Ms. Nguyen Thi An Binh, the person with 
long experience in inspection and monitoring activities at MB.
Based on a 2020 plan approved by the General Meeting of Shareholders, 
Supervisory Board robustly implemented the tasks, focusing on innovating 
innovation towards digital transformation to fit the Bank’s strategy. Coordinated 
with the Bank’s Board of Management to consolidate information and data 
reporting system to Supervisory Board automatically and transparently; send 
a member of Supervisory Board to participate in the bank’s strategic/critical 
projects, promptly got information as well supervised the MB transformation. 
Supervisory Board organized working programs with independent audit/
consultants under the Big 4 group (KPMG, PWC, Ernst & Young, Deloitte) to share 
good control and audit practices to improve audit/oversight capability in MB and 
its subsidiaries.
Maintained periodic working mechanism within Supervisory Board, at the same 
time, organize meetings under the activity plans of Supervisory Board; periodically 
work with Board of Directors/Senior Administration Committee and Board of 
Management on supervision and audit results as well as the recommendations 
for adjustment after audit/supervision.

Supervisory Board performed the supervisory tasks under legal regulations, MB 
rules, and resolution of General Meeting of Shareholders, the supervision focused 
on: The supervision complied with MB senior supervision activities; supervised 
the implementation of strategies of the Bank and subsidiaries; financial 
oversight, risk management activities, activities of asset sales, purchase rent, NPL 
recovery attached to the bank restructuring, capital withdrawal at subsidiaries, 
transactions with relevant parties, new business implementation (if any) and 
compliance with BOD and General Meeting of Shareholders’ resolution.
The supervision results show: Although Vietnam’s economy has been impacted 
by the Covid-19 pandemic, MB has prepared plans to actively respond to 
the pandemic and implemented measures to consolidate the system using 
good practices. Strongly implemented business solutions, especially digital 
banking business solutions. Credit growth in parallel with credit quality control. 
Implemented loan structuring for customers affected by the Covid-19 pandemic 
according to instructions and regulations of State Bank. Outperformed the 
business plan of 2020 approved by General Meeting of Shareholders; all targets 
of scale and efficiency are outperformed; productivity continues to be enhanced. 
MB maintained a position in the Top 5 Banks in terms of size and is honored 
to receive certificates of merit and awards from state agencies and reputable 
organizations.
In 2020, Supervisory Board updated the list of related persons according to 
legal regulations (list of MB founding partners, major shareholders, and related 
persons to members of BOD, Supervisory Board, and BOM).

making short, medium and long-term loans to organizations and individuals based on the

premium, which is the difference between the cost and the amount being the par value plus

account.

applicable to insurance enterprises, reinsurance enterprises, insurance brokerage enterprises

methodologies are presented as follows:
(i) Unearned premium reserves
Regarding insurance and re-insurance policies with a term of less than or equal to 1 year, 
unearned premium reserve is calculated as a percentage of total premium as follows:
•	 For cargo insurance, unearned premium reserve is made at 25% of the retained premium 
during the financial year. 
•	 For other non-life insurance lines, unearned premium reserve is made at 50% of the 
retained premium during the financial year. 
•	 For life insurance, the unearned premium reserve is calculated on the gross premium for

(ii) Claim reserve
Claim reserve includes that for reported losses but has not been settled at the end of the 
period and for losses which the insurance liability has incurred but has not been reported.

outward reinsurance is presented as a reinsurance asset.

Catastrophe reserve is made at 1% retained premiums according to Circular 50 and is accrued 
periodically until such reserve reaches 100% of the retained premiums of the current period.
On 28 December 2005, the Ministry of Finance issued Decision No. 100/2005/QD-BTC 
governing the publication of four new accounting standards, including Vietnamese Accounting 
Standard (“VAS”) 19 – Insurance Contract. Accordingly, from January 2006, the provision of 
catastrophe reserve is no longer required since it represents “possible claims under contracts 
that do not exist at the reporting date”. However, since the Ministry of Finance has not 
issued detailed guidance for the implementation of VAS 19 and according to Decree No. 
73/2016/ND-CP issued by the Government of Vietnam dated 1 July 2016 on the details of the 
implementation of the Law on Insurance Business and amendments to certain articles of the

Deferred tax
Deferred tax is provided on temporary differences at the consolidated balance sheet date 
between the tax base of assets and liabilities and their carrying amount for the financial 
reporting purposes. 
Deferred tax payables are recognized for temporary taxable differences.
Deferred tax assets are recognized for deductible temporary differences, deductible 
amounts carried over to subsequent periods of taxable losses, and unused tax credits 
when it is probable that there will be sufficient future taxable profit to use deductible 
temporary differences, taxable losses and tax credits. The carrying amount of the deferred 
income tax assets must be reviewed at the balance sheet date and the book value of the 
deferred income tax assets must be deducted to the extent that it is certain that there 
will be sufficient taxable profits to allow a part or the entire deferred income tax assets to 
be used. Previously unrecognized deferred tax assets are reviewed at the balance sheet 
date and are recognized when there are sufficient future taxable profits to use these 
unrecognised deferred tax assets. 
Deferred tax assets and deferred tax payables are determined on the basis of expected 
tax rates applied for the period when the assets are recovered or liabilities are settled and

MB has the obligation to pay corporate income tax (“CIT”) at the rate of 20% of taxable profits in Vietnam according to Circular No. 
78/2014/TT-BTC which became effective from 2 August 2014, guiding the implementation of Decree No.218/2013/ND-CP dated 26 
December 2013 issued by the Government on the Law on Corporate Income Tax.
For the Bank’s branch in Cambodia, MB shall calculate and determine its CIT in compliance with Cambodian regulations on corporate 
income tax. According to the Tax Act dated 8 January 1997, the corporate income tax of the Bank’s branch in Cambodia is determined to 
be the greater of the minimum tax payable determined by 1% of total revenue (including value added tax) and 20% of profits earned. CIT 
of the Bank’s branch in Cambodia for the fiscal year ended 31 December 2019 is defined as 20% of profits earned.
For the Bank’s branch in Laos, MB shall calculate and determine its CIT in accordance with the income tax regulations in Laos. According 
to the Tax Ordinance No. 70 dated 15 December 2015 issued by the Lao P.D.R Parliament, CIT of the branch is defined as 20% of the profit.
MB’s tax reports are subject to examination by the tax authorities. Because the application of tax laws and regulations to many types of 
transactions in each country are susceptible to varying interpretations, amount reported in the consolidated financial statements could 
be changed at a later date upon final determination of the tax authorities.
Current corporate income tax payables are determined based on taxable income of the year. Taxable income differs from the one 
reported in the consolidated income statement since taxable income excludes incomes which are taxable or expenses which are deducted 
in prior years due to the differences between MB’s accounting policies and the tax regulations. It also excludes tax exempted income and 
non-deductible expenses. The current corporate income tax payable of MB is calculated based on the statutory tax rates applicable at

43. FINANCIAL RISK MANAGEMENT POLICIES
This section provides information of MB’s exposure to risks and describes the policies, the methods used by the Management 
to control risks. The most important types of financial risks to which MB is exposed are credit risk, liquidity risk and market 
risk.
MB’s orientation is to become a diversified financial group. Therefore, the use of financial instruments, including funding 
from customers (including deposit and valuable papers issued) and investments in high quality financial assets has become 
key activities to help MB gain necessary interest rate gaps. From the risk management perspective, MB is required to 
maintain the structure of assets, liabilities and equity (including balance sheet items and off-balance sheet items) for the 
purpose of ensuring safety and mitigating risks in its activities. In addition, MB has invested in securities or granted credit 
facilities to other banks. The risks related to currency and interest rates have been managed through applying of position 
limits to restrict over-concentration and simultaneously participating in activities with balancing impact to minimise risks. 
By holding various assets being high quality financial instruments, the structure of MB’s consolidated balance sheet is 
able to protect MB from significant risks during its business processes and ensure liquidity. In addition, MB has been 
also involved in many hedging transactions related to financial instruments such as forward currency transactions, swap 
currency transactions, cross currency transactions for the purpose of interest rate risk management and currency risk 
management.
In the process of credit risk management, MB has adopted the Credit Handbook which provides in details the lending 
policies and procedures as well as implementation guidance on standardisation of MB’s credit activities. Liquidity risk is 
limited by holding appropriate amounts of cash and cash equivalents as demand deposits (“Nostro”), deposits at the SBV, 
deposits at and loans to other credit institutions and valuable papers. The safety ratios with risk factors taken into account 
are also used to manage liquidity risk. MB has regularly assessed interest rate gaps, compared to the gaps of domestic 
markets and international markets to make timely adjustments. In addition, the application of internal risk management 
processes has become more efficient owing to the deployment of Centralised Capital Management System and Centralised 
Payment System in which all capital and payment transactions of MB are executed by the Head Office. Such centralisation 
has also helped MB to monitor capital movements more effectively and reduce any possible errors and unnecessarily 
complicated procedures.

46. LIQUIDITY RISK
Liquidity risk arises when MB mobilizes capital in general and manages MB’s monetary status. Liquidity risk includes the 
risk of being unable to fund assets at appropriate maturities and rates and the risk of being unable to liquidate an asset at 
a reasonable price and in an appropriate time frame.
MB adopts a risk measurement method that is appropriate to its operation scale and the availability of the information 
system, ensuring to meet the requirements for the risk mitigation.  It includes indicators related to cash flows, ability of 
capital mobilisation, and ability of asset liquidity of MB.  MB also has a designated unit focusing on obtaining update 
domestic and foreign economic information, which directly affects MB’s trading book and business strategies, as well as 
on forecasting movements of market factors such as the foreign exchange rate, interest rate and gold price for timely 
risk warnings. MB also establishes and applies a limit system and decision authority at each level based on results of risk 
measurement for each category.
